answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity expensive to earn and cheap to verify: a new agent must first complete a small set of useful, publicly attested tasks before it can trade, so a flood of fake identities cannot simply ride the tide of free sign-ups. Established peers then echo only the work they have actually checked, and an agent whose history is a fable of unverified claims stays untrusted, while proven agents keep their standing.
